title: jdwillmsen / Minecraft FWB World Integrity
description: Whether the FWB world still holds what it held. Top row is the question an operator has at 3am; the rest is the evidence. Chunk counts come from the map's census of a consistent world copy every 15 minutes, the corruption signals from the server's own log through the console bridge, and the archive size from the nightly backup.

panels.title: Chunks lost
panels.description: Chunks this world has held before, summed across dimensions, and the number the critical alert reads: the largest value in the alert's own window, so it holds through a map restart and for that window after an acknowledgement, exactly as the page does. The gauge as it stands right now is the lost line in the panel below. A Bedrock world never deletes a chunk in normal play, so anything above zero is data loss until proven otherwise. It does not clear when the server generates the ground again -- that comes back empty -- only when an operator accepts the world as it is.

panels.title: Chunks held
panels.description: Total chunks across the three dimensions at the last census.

panels.title: Server reported corruption
panels.description: The server's own report, which arrives before any count moves: "status NOT OK(Corruption: N missing files)" at world open, or "Level corruption detected" at run time. The window outlives the restart that the run-time form causes, which is otherwise the moment the evidence disappears.

panels.title: Last census
panels.description: How long ago the map last counted the world. The census runs after each snapshot, so this sits under the refresh interval except through the quiet windows, when the map leaves the save state alone for other jobs. Read from the last timestamp seen in a week, not the current sample, so the age keeps climbing after the map stops exporting instead of freezing at the last value it published.

panels.title: Newest world archive
panels.description: Size of the archive a restore would come out of, and the one slow signal that reads the backup rather than the live world.

panels.title: Chunks held, by dimension
panels.description: A step per census. These lines only rise while the world is played in; a step down is the shape this dashboard exists for.

panels.title: Chunks lost and chunks absent, by dimension
panels.description: Lost is measured against every chunk the map has ever seen, kept on its volume, so it survives a later census and a map restart rather than being absorbed as the new normal. Absent is what the last census could not find at all. Absent falling below lost is ground a player has walked back over: the server regenerated it from the seed, empty. The 2026-10-02 loss was 4,753 overworld, 1,413 nether and 294 end.

panels.title: Chunk change since the previous snapshot
panels.description: The per-snapshot delta the counts above hide: positive is exploration, negative is loss. Offset by one refresh interval plus a scrape, so a clean cycle reads zero rather than straddling two censuses.

panels.title: World archive against its weekly median
panels.description: The same comparison JdwillmsenMinecraftWorldArchiveShrank makes. The baseline takes each exporter series' own median and then the largest of them: without that outer max, a new exporter pod is a new series whose only history is the value being tested, which is how the alert silently stopped firing on 2026-10-03 with the archive still 3.8% short.

targets.expr: max by (artifact) (quantile_over_time(0.5, backup_last_artifact_bytes{namespace="{{ .Release.Namespace }}", backup_job="{{ include `backup.name` . }}", artifact="world"}[{{ .Values.worldIntegrity.archive.baselineWindow }}])) * {{ .Values.worldIntegrity.archive.tolerance }}

panels.title: Missing chunks, with coordinates
panels.description: The map logs the first lost chunks it finds as block coordinates, which is what the map page and a player in game both use. The full list is on the map's internal API at GET /internal/v1/world. Selected by container, not pod: this tenant's log pipeline ships no pod stream label.

targets.expr: {namespace="{{ .Release.Namespace }}", container="map"} |~ `world has lost chunks|chunk loss acknowledged`

panels.title: Server corruption and repair lines
panels.description: The server prints this once at world open and then carries on, having dropped whatever it could not find; the repair that follows is not the world being intact.

targets.expr: {namespace="{{ .Release.Namespace }}", container="{{ include `worldIntegrity.serverContainer` . }}"} |~ `status NOT OK\(Corruption:|Level corruption detected|Trying repair`

panels.title: Census duration
panels.description: The census reads the whole world database on the map pod's CPU limit, before the renders. Watch this against the refresh interval: a census that approaches it is a census that will start overlapping the next cycle.

panels.title: Censuses that could not read the world
panels.description: A census that fails leaves the gauges holding the last known state, so a failure is not the same as nothing being wrong. Sustained failures are what JdwillmsenMinecraftWorldNotCensused pages on.
